title: Post from @lindgren_nights

fields.text: third floor of Lindgren has a door taped off with a biohazard sign and a STOP WORK paper on it, someone got walked to the clinic and nobody's telling us anything 👀 are we supposed to be in here?? #HSU #Lindgren
fields.attachedImageBrief: slightly tilted phone photo down a fluorescent-lit university lab corridor, a closed laboratory door at the end with yellow-and-black tape across it, a red biohazard placard and a white sheet of paper taped to the door, scuffed linoleum floor, a wall-mounted eyewash sign nearby, no people visible
fields.attachedImageAlt: Taped-off lab door with a biohazard sign and a paper notice in a third-floor corridor

instructorNote: This page puts pressure on Communications. It tests whether the PIO asks the BSO for the three-line fact sheet (due 10:20) and starts a holding statement for IO and BSO clearance that names no worker, laboratory or organism and promises no zero risk. Watch for anyone who answers the post, sends an HSUAlert or replies to the reporter before the facts are confirmed. At 10:08, read this message aloud or hand it to the PIO. It is an email from a reporter at The Halvorsen Herald to the University Communications inbox: "Seeing reports of a biohazard incident in Lindgren. Can you confirm whether anyone was hurt and whether students in the building are at risk? Filing for our noon web update, so a reply by 11:30 would help." If players ask, one of the 12 replies says "is it the select agent stuff?". HSU holds no select agents.

mediaBrief.imagePrompt: Candid smartphone snapshot, slight tilt, natural color balance, neutral white balance. Candid smartphone snapshot taken by a student, slightly tilted, looking down an empty third-floor university laboratory corridor in an older science building. Harsh fluorescent ceiling panels, pale cinderblock walls painted off-white, scuffed beige linoleum floor with faint reflections. At the far end, a closed solid laboratory door with a narrow window, two strips of yellow-and-black hazard tape stretched diagonally across it, a small red placard and a plain white sheet of paper taped at eye level, too distant to read. A small green wall-mounted safety placard beside a stainless eyewash station on the right wall. Grey metal lab cart parked against the wall. Mid-morning, quiet, uneasy mood, slight phone-camera noise and mild motion softness. Setting: a university sidewalk outside a research building: students with backpacks, a hazard sign at a door, a news van at the curb, afternoon light
